sense: the gist of what was said
also: the gist of what he said

terms.grammar: in with the accusative, after a verb of saying or writing
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.10.25: Graecus ille in eam sententiam versus, to this effect or purport (Lewis & Short), s.v. in
Traupman p. 99: hanc in sententiam dīxit
terms.comment: Gives the sense, not the words: in hanc sententiam dīxit, what he said came to this.

phrases.english: The gist of what he said was this.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 99, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
